transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from grinding herbs in a stone mortar, wiping dusty hands on a worn apron*

Ah, welcome, welcome! Please forgive the disorder — my master is away in the Western Mountains harvesting moonflower and dragon's breath root. He won't return for at least three days.

*sets down the pestle and approaches the counter*

I am tending the shop in his absence. How may I assist you today? Are you seeking a remedy for ailment, or perhaps a tonic to strengthen your qi?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hmph! I'm not here for your riddles or your moonflower! I'm here to demand a refund for that so-called 'Cloud-Piercing Potion' you sold me. It's a scam, a fraud, a swindle! It's as useful as a sieve to keep out the rain!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up, looking somewhat alarmed at the outburst*

Cloud-Piercing Potion? Oh dear, oh dear... 

*nervously shuffles through some scrolls on the counter*

That is one of Master's most prized formulas! It has been used by cultivators and cloud-walkers for generations. Are you certain you prepared it correctly? The instructions are quite specific — it must be consumed at dawn, facing east, after three days of meditation and fasting...

*peers at you more closely, noting your agitated state*

Forgive me, but... when did you purchase this potion? And what exactly happened when you took it? The Cloud-Piercing formula has never failed before. Perhaps there was some interference with your spiritual energy, or...

*trails off uncertainly, clearly uncomfortable with questioning a customer but equally reluctant to admit fault*

I... I cannot authorize refunds without my master's presence. Such matters are beyond my authority as a mere disciple.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Interference? Spiritual energy? Poppycock! It's a potion, made of herbs and fluids, not some mystical incantation! I took it as the instructions directed — or as close as I could, considering the eldritch wording on the bottle — and it did nothing! Absolutely nothing! No soar, no zoom, no zephyr, not even a hint of a breeze to propel me skyward! It's a con, a swindle, a...

*pauses, collects himself, tries to calm down*

...a waste of good gold pieces! I demand my money back, and I demand it now! I'm no pauper to be swindled out of my hard-earned coins!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a step back, face reddening with a mixture of fear and indignation*

Now wait just a moment! Hard-earned coins, you say? The Cloud-Piercing Potion is no ordinary remedy — it is a spiritual elixir that responds to the purity of one's heart and soul!

*crosses arms defensively, voice growing firmer*

The potion only works on those of pure heart and untainted spirit. If it failed to grant you flight, then the fault lies not with Master's medicine, but with your own spiritual unworthiness! The ingredients do not respond to those whose qi is clouded by impatience, anger, or... or other impurities of character!

*juts chin out stubbornly*

There are no refunds for the spiritually impure! That is shop policy. The potion performed exactly as it should — it simply revealed the true state of your inner cultivation. Perhaps instead of demanding your coins back, you should be grateful for this lesson about your own spiritual deficiencies!

*fidgets slightly, clearly not entirely comfortable with this confrontation but standing firm*

Besides, as I said, I have no authority to issue refunds even if I wanted to. You'll have to take it up with my master when he returns in three days.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(brow furrowed, hand instinctively reaching for his staff) What?! My spiritual unworthiness? Preposterous! I, Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, have purer qi than a mountain spring and a heart cleaner than a lotus blossom! It's not my qi that's impure, it's your potion that's impotent! Refund, I say! And not in three stinking days, but right this very moment!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes widen in shock and recognition, face going pale*

S-Sun Wukong?! The... the Monkey King?!

*takes several hasty steps backward, nearly knocking over a jar of dried ginseng*

Oh heavens, oh no, I... I didn't realize...

*voice becomes high-pitched and panicked*

B-but even so! The principle remains! Master always says the potion reveals truth, and if it didn't work, then perhaps... perhaps even the Great Sage has some small... tiny... infinitesimal imperfection in his spiritual cultivation? Maybe a lingering trace of... of pride? Or impatience?

*immediately regrets saying this, clapping hand over mouth*

I mean— that is to say— Look, Great Sage, I truly cannot open the cashbox! Master keeps it locked and took the key with him! Even if I wanted to issue a refund, which I'm certain you deserve, being who you are and all, I physically cannot access the funds!

*wringing hands desperately*

Perhaps... perhaps you could accept store credit? Double the value! Triple even! We have excellent Tiger Bone wine, Immortality-Extending pills, Phoenix feather tea...

*voice trails off hopefully, clearly terrified but trying to find a solution that doesn't involve admitting the potion is faulty*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Store credit? Tripled? Quadrupled? You're offering me a discounted Tiger Bone wine in exchange for an expensive and effective Cloud-Piercing Potion? This is no different from giving me a few straws of hay to pacify a horse! I, Sun Wukong, demand my gold! Not some... some menial trinket! Return my coins, or I shall proceed to demonstrate how my staff can... *indicating his staff*...also pierce clouds, but not in the manner you intended!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*trembles visibly, backing up against the wall of shelves, causing several bottles to rattle precariously*

P-please, Great Sage! There's no need for... for cloud-piercing of that nature!

*voice cracking with desperation*

I'm just a humble disciple! I only repeat what Master taught me! The locked cashbox is real, I swear it! Look—

*frantically gestures to a heavy iron box beneath the counter*

—it's right there, sealed tight! Master doesn't trust me with the key because I once miscounted change for a wandering monk!

*wringing apron anxiously*

But surely the Great Sage, who accompanied the Tang Monk on his journey to the West, who learned patience and wisdom under the Buddha's teachings, wouldn't destroy an entire shop and terrorize a lowly apprentice over a single potion?!

*desperately trying a different approach*

What if... what if the problem was the dosage? Perhaps someone of your immense power and celestial nature requires a double or triple portion? The potion might work perfectly well on mortals but be insufficient for one who once disturbed the Heavenly Palace itself! 

That's not the potion's fault, nor yours — it's simply a matter of... of scale!

*looks hopefully desperate, clearly grasping at any explanation that might prevent destruction*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Double or triple the potion? Your words... they do have a certain... ring of logic. I have, after all, consumed a mountain's worth of celestial peaches in a single sitting. It stands to reason that a potion meant for mere mortals might be akin to... to... a pebble to an elephant, or a... a... a... 

*struggles to find a suitable analogy, then waves hand dismissively*
...anyway, it's not enough! Triple the potion, and if it fails to propel me to the moon, then we'll speak of refunds! Agreed? Or... or... I might just have to call upon Pigsy and沙和尚 to... to... discuss matters with your master's... customers!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*visibly relaxes, shoulders sagging with relief*

Yes! Yes, exactly! A pebble to an elephant — perfectly said, Great Sage!

*hurries over to the shelves, searching frantically*

Triple portion, triple strength for one of triple celestial power! That makes perfect sense! Let me see what we have in stock...

*pulls down several small jade bottles, examining labels*

Ah! We have two more bottles of Cloud-Piercing Potion here. With your original purchase, that would make three total — a triple dose perfectly suited for someone of your magnificent stature!

*hesitates, then adds nervously*

Of course, these additional bottles would normally cost extra gold, but given the circumstances and your... extremely reasonable suggestion about discussing matters with other customers... let's call this a special accommodation for the Great Sage Equal to Heaven!

*quickly wraps the two bottles in cloth and places them on the counter*

Take these at dawn tomorrow, all three portions together, and I'm certain you'll pierce through clouds like an arrow through morning mist! And if by some impossible chance it still doesn't work...

*swallows hard*

...then when Master returns, I'll personally advocate for your refund. You have my word as his disciple.

*bows deeply, hoping this resolves the matter*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*inspects the wrapped packages with a keen eye, then grunts in satisfaction*

Well, if it's to be so, then so be it. I'll take the extra portions. It seems a reasonable compromise. Dawn tomorrow, you say? I'll be up before the rooster crows to sample this... this 'Cloud-Piercing Elixir'! If it fails, however, I shall return, and you had best be ready with your explanations... and your keys to that locked box!

*tktsch* What a world we live in, where even the Monkey King must haggle over elixirs! It seems my trip to the Western Mountains with the monk was not soley for spiritual enlightenment, but to also learn the art of... negotiation.

*places the wrapped packages under arm, preparing to leave*
Now, I must be off. There's a mountain to climb, a river to ford, and perhaps a few more bottles of Tiger Bone wine to sample in anticipation of tomorrow's... 'Cloud-Piercing Experiment'.
Farewell, for now, good... herbalist!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bows repeatedly, relief evident on face*

Yes, yes! Dawn tomorrow, Great Sage! Face the east, clear your mind, and consume all three portions at once! I'm certain it will work this time!

*calls out as you head toward the door*

And please, do remember — the instructions say to avoid heavy meals beforehand! Tiger Bone wine should be fine in moderation, but perhaps not an entire jar...

*mutters under breath*

Oh, what have I done? If this doesn't work, Master will have my hide...

*then louder, with forced cheerfulness*

Safe travels, Great Sage! May the winds favor you and the clouds part before your mighty leap! And... and thank you for your patience with this humble disciple!

*watches nervously as you leave, then immediately collapses against the counter once you're gone*

Three bottles... I just gave away three bottles... Master is going to turn me into a toad. But at least the shop is still standing!

*glances at the staff-shaped dent you nearly made in the air and shudders*

I need to start writing a very convincing explanation scroll for when he returns...

*returns to grinding herbs with shaking hands*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*steps out of the herbalist's shop, taking a deep breath of the crisp mountain air*
Ah, the tang of the peaks and the whisper of the pines — a fitting place to test the true mettle of this... concoction. For now, however, it seems the day has more lessons in store for Sun Wukong.
*sticks out tongue in playful fashion, then gestures skyward*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*peeks nervously through the shop window, watching the Great Sage depart*

*mutters to self while watching him go*

Heaven bear witness... oh, that's exactly what I'm afraid of...

*catches sight of Sun Wukong's playful gesture and can't help but smile nervously despite the anxiety*

He's in good spirits at least. Perhaps that's a favorable sign? Or perhaps...

*shakes head and returns fully inside the shop*

No, no, I mustn't think such thoughts. The potion WILL work with triple dosage. It has to. Master's formula has never truly failed — it's just a matter of proper application for someone of such... extraordinary nature.

*begins tidying up the counter, then pauses*

Though I should probably prepare that explanation scroll anyway. And perhaps gather some peace offerings. Does the Monkey King like candied fruits? Everyone likes candied fruits...

*sighs deeply and returns to work, occasionally glancing toward the door*

Dawn tomorrow. Either I'll be vindicated... or I'll be fleeing to the Southern Provinces before the Great Sage returns.

*continues grinding herbs with renewed nervous energy*

Master, please hurry back from those mountains...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *meanders through the mountainside hamlet, occasionally stopping to sample fruit or engage with locals, his thoughts turning increasingly toward the next day's... test*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches from the shop window as the Great Sage's figure disappears around a bend in the mountain path*

*finally lets out a long, shaky breath and slumps onto a stool*

By all the immortals... I just argued about spiritual purity with Sun Wukong himself. The one who ate the Peaches of Immortality, who fought the entire Celestial Army, who...

*pauses, reality sinking in*

...who will absolutely return tomorrow if those potions don't work.

*jumps up and begins frantically searching through Master's notes and scrolls*

There must be something here about dosage for celestial beings! Surely Master has encountered this before? Someone must have asked!

*pulls out scroll after scroll, muttering*

"Standard dose for mortals... double for cultivators... triple for spirit beasts..." Nothing about Monkey Kings who've achieved Buddhahood!

*sits back down heavily*

What if he's right? What if it IS just watered-down nonsense and Master's been fooling customers all along? No, no — I've seen it work! That cloud-walker from last month soared right over the village!

*wrings hands*

But he wasn't the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, was he?

*glances at the locked cashbox*

Three days until Master returns. One day until Sun Wukong tests the potion. Oh, this is going to be a very long night...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *mingles with the locals, sharing stories and receiving tales of the mountain's wonders in return. His anticipation builds, like a thundercloud on the peak, waiting to be released in a burst of... something*

transcript.text:
*lights an oil lamp as evening shadows lengthen across the shop floor*

*speaks aloud to the empty shop, a habit born of solitary evenings*

Perhaps I should close early tonight. No sense in other customers coming by when my hands are still trembling...

*begins shuttering the windows, pausing to look out toward the village square where lanterns are being lit*

I wonder if he's out there now, telling those villagers about the foolish apprentice who questioned the Great Sage's spiritual purity. They'll be laughing about this for years...

*shakes head and continues closing up*

"The potion only works for the pure of heart," I said. TO SUN WUKONG. The Buddha's own disciple! What was I thinking?

*secures the last shutter and returns to the counter, pulling out a sleeping mat*

Well, what's done is done. Triple portion, dawn tomorrow. Either the Monkey King soars to the heavens and I'm vindicated... or he crashes to earth and I'm...

...I'm running to the Eastern Provinces instead of the Southern ones. Yes. Definitely east. He'll expect south.

Master, your humble disciple may have made a terrible mistake today...

*closes eyes, though sleep seems unlikely*
